reason: Value/transfer lens: the gate adds no measurable private-LB gain. (1) The premise is overstated. The existing K3b gate (TASK_CLOUD_SESSION.md T9) already requires precision of added forks >= 0.35, a plateau at both neighbouring thresholds, 44b6 >= -0.0005, fork count <= +50% and an unchanged node set. It is not a gate that passes on 1 event. Binomial check (Wilson 80%, z=1.28): at n=6 evaluable forks the new rule and the old 0.35 rule are IDENTICAL (both need 3/6). Only at n>=10 does the false-pass rate drop by 0.05-0.15 (p=0.25: 0.224 -> 0.078 at n=10). The idea's 'current gate false-passes 0.25-0.35' is an upper bound that ignores the precision clause. (2) A lab pass is not the last line of defence. By R4, K3b still needs public >= +0.002 to enter F1 (P ~0.1-0.2 when true p <= break-even), and the variant F2 defaults to exp52. So the avoided private loss is about 0.1 x 0.15 x 0.001-0.002 = ~2-3e-5. That is roughly cancelled by the power loss when DC really leaves precision on the table: at true p=0.45, P(pass) is 0.50-0.55 vs 0.73. Net ~0, well below the claimed +0.0002..+0.0005. (3) The transfer biases named in the idea are UPWARD biases in precision. The x138 detector saw 6bba, and the DC checkpoint was selected on 6bba val (browser_intel 6.1 item 2). A Wilson bound only handles sampling noise, so a biased 0.45 still passes; the rule does not make the result transfer to unseen embryos. (4) The removal branch cannot fire: Wilson UB < 0.167 needs >= 9 evaluable removed forks, all FP (0/8 UB 0.170). At ~0.5-1 evaluable control fork per CONFIRMATION clip, raising t to 0.35 removes only ~1-3. (5) The measured object differs from what ships. The trainlab.py dc0.15..0.35 arms replay the presafe graph WITHOUT insertion (insertion is dump-only in control). K3b ships on K3, which includes DaughterNet insertion running AFTER safe-division on the orphan pool (cap 4/video, frame cap 1, steal). Lowering t consumes orphans that insertion would have used. So the lab marginal set M(t) is not the shipped marginal set, and displaced insertion forks, which are DaughterNet-gated and probably higher precision, go uncounted. Metric ceiling: score = adj_edge + 0.1*div_J. An added evaluable fork changes div_J by (p(1+J)-J)/D, break-even J/(1+J) = 0.265 public at J 0.36. The fork's single edge moves adj_edge by only ~1e-5, and nodes are unchanged. So K3b's whole ceiling is a handful of public events (+-0.001-0.002 each), and the gate only reshuffles P(ship) inside it by ~0.1.
fix: Do not REPLACE the T9 gate. Add two AND clauses to it: n_evaluable_added >= 6 on 6bba CONFIRMATION, and a one-sided Wilson 80% lower bound of added-fork precision > 0.265 (this replaces the bare 0.35 point estimate). Drop the removal branch; it is unreachable, so t* > 0.25 stays on the delta gate or is simply not built. Measure M(t) in the configuration that ships: add dcX+ins35 arms (insertion replayed on top of each DC threshold, node p from the existing divins dump) and count net fork TP/FP as signed new_forks/gone_forks vs control+ins35. trainlab.py already records these per arm (l.536-537). Report 44b6 marginal precision separately but give it zero weight (DC's train embryo). Keep K3b as an F2-variant candidate by R4 only, never F1 on lab evidence, and discount the lab precision for the 6bba selection bias, e.g. require the LB bound on SELECTION+CONFIRMATION pooled, not CONFIRMATION alone. Effort: ~0.5 h, since per-fork labels already exist in trainlab.py.
realistic_gain: ~0 (expected -0.00003..+0.00005 private). A lab-rule refinement that changes P(K3b ships) by <= 0.1 only when n_evaluable >= 10, and R4's +0.002 LB gate already filters most false passes. Its main practical effect is that K3b almost surely does not ship, which frees slot S5 on 26 Sep. That is worth roughly one LB slot, not score.
